episode_row: bpm feature slowed prediction >5 min → stale heartbeat → HC failure DM

commits.subject: fix(features): vectorize bpm cumsum — restore prediction-cycle latency
commits.body:
PR #4 (deployed 17:24 ET 2026-04-29) used .transform(lambda s: s.cumsum().shift(1).fillna(0))
in the bpm computation. On the prod 1.5M-PA frame, that lambda-per-group pattern
pushed compute_all_features past the 5-min heartbeat-watchdog threshold
(stale=True at 17:30:01 ET, 330s old, fired Healthchecks failure DM).

Replaces the lambda with vectorized:
  groupby().cumsum() - current_value
which is bit-exact equivalent (verified: max abs diff 0.0 across 65k paired
rows on real 2026 data) but avoids per-group Python overhead.

Timing on 33k-PA 2026 frame:
  Vectorized (this commit):            1.77s
  Lambda (PR#4 / experiment-class):    5.53s
  → 3.1× faster

Extrapolated to prod's 1.5M frame: ~80s vs ~250s. The 250s was right at the
5-min heartbeat threshold; the 80s is comfortably under.

The BatterPitcherMatchupExperiment.modify_features still uses the slower
lambda variant — left untouched since the experiment is now idempotent (early-
returns when column already exists from compute_all_features) and only runs
in batch contexts (Phase 1/2 audits) where 5-min heartbeat doesn't apply.

846/846 non-slow tests pass.
